topic: Karp's Conjecture 4 on fractional-degree Legendre Turan inequalities
title: A rational counterexample to Karp's fractional-degree Legendre Turán conjecture

creators.name: Wenlin Zhang
creators.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

abstract: Karp's Conjecture 4 in his 2011 SF21 presentation (physical PDF page 52, repeated on pages 53–54, https://math.nist.gov/~DLozier/SF21/SF21slides/Karp.pdf) fails at mu=3/2, delta=63/64, y=4095/4096: exact rational series bounds give a Legendre Turánian at most -97/5000, with all three degrees positive. The standard zero-balanced hypergeometric expansion also gives counterexamples at every positive noninteger central degree, for shifts sufficiently close to one. For each fixed admissible degree and shift, the Turánian is positive near both ends of 0<y<1; hence the explicit counterexample lies between at least two interior zeros.
summary: A rational counterexample refutes Karp's fractional-degree conjecture. Written endpoint analysis proves positivity near both endpoints at fixed parameters and negative interior values for shifts near one at every positive noninteger central degree.
posing_locator: Conjecture 4, physical PDF page 52, repeated on pages 53–54

coverage.formal_statement: Negation of the fully quantified strict comparison for real mu>0, 0<delta<1 and 0<y<1
written_proofs: Explicit counterexample using exact series enclosures
Failure of the non-strict comparison with all degrees positive; this weaker comparison is not separately asserted in the posing source
Positivity near zero for each fixed admissible parameter pair
T(mu,delta,y) = sin(pi*delta)^2/pi^2 * log(1-y)^2 + O(abs(log(1-y))) as y tends to one for each fixed admissible pair
For every positive noninteger mu, a fixed interior y_mu gives negative values for every delta sufficiently close to one from below
At least two distinct interior zeros for the rational parameter pair
not_covered: Classification on positive-valued or suitable zero-free regions
General strict-log-concavity polynomial conjectures, the discrete-to-continuous shift conjecture, and the Prekopa-Ninh comparison in the posing slide deck
coverage.sibling_attribution: Karp, arXiv:1203.1482v1, Lemma 3 gives the geometric equality boundary up to a constant factor; Theorem 1 proves the strict-log-concavity alpha=beta=1 positive-coefficient case. These prior polynomial results are credited, not presented as new.
